objective.text: Pass serialized constructor data explicitly instead of assuming one handle return becomes the next input.

difficulty.rationale: Define durable data transfer explicitly between independently serialized jobs.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: The first chained job returns a generated report ID from handle(). The second job expects that return value to appear automatically in its constructor input. Why is that design incomplete?

options.text: The report ID is passed only when both jobs use the same queue name.
options.rationale: Queue routing does not turn a handler return into another job’s constructor argument.
options.misconception: Queue routing does not turn a handler return into another job’s constructor argument.

options.text: The report ID is automatically passed, but only if it is a string.
options.rationale: There is no built-in return-value pipeline restricted to string results.
options.misconception: There is no built-in return-value pipeline restricted to string results.

options.text: The constructor runs again with the previous result only after a failed attempt.
options.rationale: Retry does not establish this automatic data-transfer contract either.
options.misconception: Retry does not establish this automatic data-transfer contract either.

options.text: Chains control execution order; they do not automatically pass handle return values into successor constructors.
options.rationale: Successors are serialized jobs with their own inputs. Persist shared state or explicitly construct subsequent work with the needed identifier.

explanation.summary: Successors are serialized jobs with their own inputs. Persist shared state or explicitly construct subsequent work with the needed identifier.
